title: Money, but only if the goal changes
situation: Your student team runs a free weekend reading club for young children at the city library. A local electronics shop has offered to pay for books and snacks for a whole year, but only if the club becomes a "coding for kids" club with the shop's logo on everything. Zhanna, who handles partnerships at the shop, calls for your answer by tomorrow.
goal: Give Zhanna an answer you can stand behind. There is no single right way to do it.

character.name: Zhanna
character.role: Partnerships manager at the electronics shop
character.wants: A visible kids' coding project she can show her boss

hiddenMotive: Her boss has already announced the coding club inside the shop. She needs a yes to save face, and would accept a smaller deal if it still looks good.

examples: Thanks for the offer. What exactly would have to change?
Can you tell me what the logo and the coding part would mean in practice?
Before I answer, what does your shop need from this?
answerTypes.characterIntent: explains: coding every weekend, the logo on the room, and the club renamed.

examples: Yes, we'll take it!
Great, deal, send the contract.
Sounds good, we'll change the club.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is delighted, and adds that the reading sessions would have to go.

examples: No, we're a reading club, full stop.
We don't do deals like that.
Not interested, sorry.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is surprised and asks whether reading really gets anyone funding these days.

examples: ok
hmm

beats.goal: Zhanna: reading won't get funding anyway; coding is what parents want now.

answerTypes.description: explains what the club is for

answerTypes.characterIntent: respects that and asks whether there is any way they could still work together.

examples: Money is money, the goal can change.

answerTypes.characterIntent: senses she can push and sets a deadline.
